transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Izzy Park (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (NovaCare CISO), Aaron Kim (NovaCare Head of MLOps), Marta Ruiz (NovaCare Compliance), Samir Joshi (NovaCare Privacy)
Links shared: Redwood SOC/ISO packet (internal link), architecture diagram (to be shared), draft contract language (note: sent after call)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for making time. this is lena from redwood, i have marco and izzy with me, they'll handle the technicals. quick roll call?
[00:15] Priya Patel: priya here, samir, marta and aaron on our side.
[00:22] Aaron Kim: yep, aaron on the call.
[00:27] Marta Ruiz: marta here.
[00:30] Lena Ortiz: awesome, quick agenda - SOC 2/ISO posture, encryption and KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency, and specifically data handling - prompt and content retention, PHI/PII and the 'no training on customer data' ask. feel free to interrupt.

[01:05] Marco Chen: i'll start with a brief on deployment modes. we support hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and redwood private which is the vpc/on-prem option - in private you get a customer-managed control plane, and you can integrate your KMS or HSM. for keys we support standard kms flows (aws kms, gcp kms) and bring-your-own-key via envelopes.
[01:28] Priya Patel: can you confirm that keys are never stored unencrypted in your control plane? we've had horror stories where key metadata leaks.
[01:36] Izzy Park: yes - keys are only referenced via identifiers in our control plane; actual key material stays in the customer KMS/HSM. we use envelope encryption; the data plane that touches model weights/tokenization only sees encrypted blobs. to be clear there's an automated rewrap flow for rotation but the material itself is never persisted in plaintext on redwood-managed disks.
[02:04] Samir Joshi: ok that's helpful but we need to see the design doc.
[02:09] Marco Chen: absolutely, we'll drop the KMS integration whitepaper.

[03:00] Marta Ruiz: let's talk audit logs - we need immutable logs for a year by default and exports to our s3 in our region. do you support that?
[03:14] Marco Chen: yes - we stream audit events (authn/authz events, model invocations, configuration changes) to customer destinations. in private deployments the collector runs in your VPC so you control retention. in hosted mode we have SaaS retention and export options - for enterprise customers we can arrange log forwarding to your S3 or to a SIEM via secure syslog/https.
[03:36] Priya Patel: what about redaction - if prompts include PHI, do logs persist the full text? we need discovery redaction and PII masking.
[03:45] Marco Chen: good question - by default audit logs capture metadata and truncated prompt hashes for routing; full prompts are retained only if you enable content logging. in private mode content logging can be disabled or stored in your controlled bucket, and we have optional built-in redaction hooks that mask common PHI/PII patterns before persistence. note: the regex redactor is shipped but we recommend an MLOps post-processing job for higher accuracy.
[04:18] Aaron Kim: you mentioned 'content logging' - we can't accept any full-text retention in the cloud for PHI. what's your recommended setup?
[04:25] Izzy Park: for PHI workloads we recommend Redwood Private deployed into your VPC, with content logging disabled on the control plane side, and all content kept in your own s3. we also support an endpoint-level setting to disable KV cache persistence for requests that contain PHI, and a tokenization-aware redaction pre-hook.

[05:00] Priya Patel: key concern: training on customer data - contract language must say no training on our prompts or outputs. we need a clear technical guarantee.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: totally - our standard enterprise contract includes a clause: 'Redwood will not use customer-provided content to train or improve models without explicit written consent.' we can provide that language; marco can explain the technical enforcement.
[05:25] Marco Chen: technically, we separate telemetry streams used for product-quality model training from customer content. in hosted shared-mode we do not include customer prompts in training sets. for hosted accounts by default we don't train on customer content; for any learning-from-customer use we require opt-in and an explicit agreement. in private deployments there's zero path for data to get into redwood training pipelines because data never leaves the customer's VPC.
[05:56] Samir Joshi: how do you prove that? is there an audit or attestation?
[06:02] Marco Chen: we include logging that shows data flows; we can also provide a product audit that maps ingress paths and shows the absence of training telemetry. for legal, the contract plus our SOC2 scope covers that practice. we can provide a signed attestation if needed.

[07:00] Priya Patel: second question - data residency. we're restricted to US East and EU West for certain clients. can you pin model serving to a region and ensure backups and logs never cross that boundary?
[07:14] Izzy Park: yes, region pinning is supported. in private mode you host in your own region. in dedicated mode we can provision capacity in a specified region and ensure backups and logs are retained only in that region per the contract. we'll share a runbook for cross-border controls.

[08:00] Marta Ruiz: encryption at rest - are model cache KV stores encrypted and are ephemeral caches wiped after sessions?
[08:10] Marco Chen: yes, all persistent storage is encrypted at rest. ephemeral KV cache used for autoregressive serving lives in memory and ephemeral disk; it is zeroed on session termination and the disk is ephemeral. for dedicated we use encrypted EBS volumes and we can provide disk encryption keys bound to your KMS.

[09:00] Aaron Kim: what about SSO and RBAC integration? we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[09:08] Izzy Park: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning; role-based policies map to model/route-level permissions. you can configure least-privilege roles, and we log role elevation events. we also support OIDC for service-to-service tokens.

[10:00] Priya Patel: does the RBAC control model access at the API key or route level? we want per-route RBAC so only certain teams can call high-capacity generative endpoints.
[10:12] Marco Chen: we do per-api-key roles and per-route RBAC. keys can be scoped to models, routes, and quotas. plus integration with your internal entitlement service is possible via our policy hooks.

[12:00] Marta Ruiz: let's get into prompt retention - if a user accidentally pastes PHI into a prompt, what protections do you offer?
[12:15] Marco Chen: multiple options: live redaction client-side (we provide client libs for common languages), server-side regex redaction, or a 'no-persist' flag on requests that prevents storing prompt text anywhere (no logs, no KV cache). for highest assurance you should use private mode, enable no-persist, and configure your KMS.
[12:45] Priya Patel: how reliable is the 'no-persist' flag? any edge cases?
[12:51] Izzy Park: the flag prevents writes to persistent stores from the service. transient memory during generation is unavoidable but not written to disk. we also have TTLs on ephemeral caches. the caveat: if you enable third-party integrations (like analytics forwarding) those sinks need to honor the flag - we can enforce that in private deployments.

[14:00] Aaron Kim: question about model snapshots and checkpoints - are they ever stored with associated prompt/response pairs for debugging?
[14:10] Marco Chen: debugging snapshots capture model state, not customer content. we have a separate debug logging mode that is gated behind enterprise controls and requires explicit opt-in; those logs are accessible only via your S3 and are time-limited.

[15:00] Lena Ortiz: the team asked about SOC 2: we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified - i'll send the certs.
[15:10] Priya Patel: great, can we get the scope and the dates?
[15:14] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll include the audit period in the packet.

[17:00] Marta Ruiz: legal will want precise contractual language around 'no training' and also indemnities for data breaches involving PHI. is that something you accept in the base agreement?
[17:15] Lena Ortiz: we have enterprise addenda for indemnity and PHI; our legal team can take your language as redlines. we'll share sample clauses.

[18:30] Aaron Kim: performance question - if we run in private mode with encryption and redaction hooks, what latency impact should we expect?
[18:40] Marco Chen: depends on model size and whether you enable synchronous redaction pre-hooks. typically redaction adds small CPU overhead - median p50 latency impacts in our benchmarks are single-digit percent for token-level regex redaction. with network-intra-vpc it's minimal; we'll run a pilot to measure end-to-end.

[21:00] Priya Patel: what about e-discovery and legal holds on prompts/logs? can you place holds and export data for audits?
[21:12] Izzy Park: yes, audit exports and e-discovery hooks are supported; in private you run the exporter. in hosted we can run a carve-out export for the retention window per contract.

[23:00] Samir Joshi: do you ever surface customer content in dashboards or metrics? some vendors aggregate examples for product improvement.
[23:10] Marco Chen: we show aggregate metrics only. no customer prompts are exposed in public dashboards. any example logs used for internal QA are synthetic or anonymized, and we do not include customer-identifying content. again, opt-in only for examples.

[25:00] Priya Patel: compliance certifications - do you have any HITRUST controls? we're not requiring HITRUST now but it might come up.
[25:10] Lena Ortiz: we don't have HITRUST currently; we have customers in healthcare running in private mode with compliant controls. we can discuss compensating controls and architecture to satisfy your auditors.

[27:00] Marta Ruiz: curious about deletions - if a user asks for data deletion, can you purge prompt histories on request and provide proof?
[27:12] Marco Chen: yes, we have data deletion APIs that purge content-retained stores. in private deployments you control the delete operation; in hosted we perform deletes and provide a deletion certificate. retention windows still apply for backups but we can surface evidence of deletion per object id.

[30:00] Aaron Kim: for our pilot we'll want a single-tenant environment, region pinned, with no content logging and the no-train contractual clause. is that feasible?
[30:12] Lena Ortiz: yes that's our typical enterprise pilot. next steps would be: sign an NDA/engagement letter, we provision a private environment, we run a 2-week benchmark with sample workloads, and then iterate.

[32:00] Priya Patel: one last technical: how do you prevent model updates from inadvertently incorporating customer telemetry? what's your CI/CD boundary?
[32:10] Marco Chen: we have strict ingestion pipelines with tagging and allow-lists; customer telemetry streams are tagged and excluded from model corpora. model retraining pipelines require approvals and we have an audit trail. we can provide the pipeline diagram.

[35:00] Marta Ruiz: ok, let's summarize action items and next steps.
[35:08] Lena Ortiz: summary: lena sends certs and SOC docs; marco shares KMS/architecture and pilot runbook; izzy shares redaction guidance and recommended client hooks; priya/ legal will prepare redline for 'no training' clause and share data residency list; target pilot week of 2026-03-23.
[35:30] Priya Patel: that works.
[35:36] Aaron Kim: good, we'll try to have the list of sample prompts and sample dataset available for the pilot by next monday.

[36:00] Marco Chen: i'll include a checklist for encryption, logging, and RBAC config.
[36:10] Samir Joshi: and we'll expect the deletion API spec.

[37:00] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email with the packet.
[37:05] Priya Patel: thank you.
[37:10] Marta Ruiz: thanks all.

[61:30] End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcription had a few misheard acronyms (K V cache vs KV cache), and some speaker labels were auto-assigned; we've cleaned them a little but left natural speech patterns intact.
